text:
maria: quick thread — proposing we split the console_events read model out of the raw_ingest table into a dedicated read_model_v2 to improve dashboard query latency and make rollouts safer. TL;DR: dual-write, small canary shard, chunked backfill via kafka snapshots, read adapter that can route to v2 by feature-flag.
simon: strong +1 on separating concerns. a few Qs: how do we keep the console UX consistent during backfill? and what's the plan for historical queries?
alex: for historical we can do chunked replays of compacted kafka topics (topic: console-events-compact) and also snapshot export for very old data. replays are idempotent if we include origin_event_id dedupe.
ben: infra concerns — dual-write increases producer latency. we should measure p50 added per request. also need a circuit-breaker fallback so console still queries raw_ingest if v2 is unavailable.
maria: agreed. proposed safety: 
- dual-write behind feature-flag (config flag: console.read_model.v2.dual_write)
- dual-write done async with bounded queue, producers continue on timeout
- read adapter with route precedence: if feature-flag & shard in canary -> query v2 else fallback to raw_ingest
- backlog replayer job with chunking and rate-limit + checkpointing

simon: can we avoid heavy joins in v2 by pre-aggregating per-route daily metrics? some dashboard panels do many group-bys.
alex: yes. schema idea: store event envelope flattened columns we use in console (tenant_id, route_id, route_label, event_kind, timestamp, metric_tags[]) and maintain materialized daily aggregates for heavy dashboards. store raw payload in separate column for ad-hoc debug queries.
ben: ops pieces: need migration runbook and a k8s job to do replay. we should also add an alert on consumer lag and a dashboard for per-shard ingest rate. if replay fails, have a safe resume token.
maria: sketch of SQL for v2 table (first pass):
```sql
CREATE TABLE console_events_v2 (
  tenant_id UUID,
  event_ts TIMESTAMPTZ,
  route_id TEXT,
  event_kind TEXT,
  route_label TEXT,
  metric_value DOUBLE PRECISION,
  payload JSONB,
  origin_event_id TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, origin_event_id)
);
```
This keeps dedupe simple for replay. payload is optional for storage tiering.
simon: primary key choice ok for idempotency but watch PK bloat. for PG we might prefer a different clustering/index strategy. for ClickHouse we'd denormalize differently. need storage tech decision.
alex: recommendation: keep v2 in Postgres for now for small tenants + quick rollouts, and push long-term cold/archive to ClickHouse via connector. Avoid cross-system queries in dashboards by moving most panels to v2 aggregates.
ben: rollout plan (ops minded):
1) add read adapter + feature flag (no schema change)
2) enable dual-write in canary tenant set A (5 tenants) behind flag
3) run replayer on canary partitions for last 30d and verify dashboards
4) expand dual-write + replay to 10% tenants
5) run full historical backfill in parallel with throttling and monitoring
6) once stable, flip default routing to v2 for read-mostly dashboards, keep fallback window for 2w

maria: example feature-flag toggle command (devctl):
```bash
devctl feature set console.read_model.v2.dual_write --tenants=canaryA --enabled=true
```
ben: we should also add a canary query compare job that runs a sample set of dashboard queries against raw_ingest and v2 and diffs rowcounts / top-k values nightly. add regression alerts if mismatch >1% or result latency delta >50ms.

alex: perf/backfill note: chunk size 100k events per job and parallelize by tenant_id hash. include backoff when PG CPU >70%.

maria: ownerships: 
- simon: runbook & read-adapter routing logic
- alex: schema + replay tooling
- ben: infra + monitoring + rollout gating
I'll create PRs for schema + adapter and a draft runbook.

ingest-bot: snapshot available: s3://redwood-backups/console-events-snap/2024-06-12.tar.gz (size: 42GB)
simon: perfect — I'll use that for a dry-run.
maria: ok next steps: simon please create the runbook draft and pick 5 canary tenants; alex open schema PR; ben wire up alerts. sync tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
ben: noted. added to my queue.
alex: starting schema PR today.
maria: thanks all, closing thread for now — we'll move to PR comments for details. :rocket:
